definitions.gloss: taking out one's anger on someone else; misdirected anger; venting frustration on an innocent party
definitions.explanation: directing anger or frustration at someone or something unrelated to the actual source of one's frustration

examples.english: Don't take it out on me.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}のストレスを{家族|かぞく}に{八|や}つ{当|あ}たりしてしまった。
examples.english: I took out my work stress on my family.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{機嫌|きげん}が{悪|わる}いと{周|まわ}りに{八|や}つ{当|あ}たりする{癖|くせ}がある。
examples.english: He has a habit of taking his bad mood out on others.

notes:
FORMS:
{八|やっ}つ (eight) + {当|あ}たり (hitting) → hitting out in all eight directions
The name suggests striking out blindly in all directions.
{八|や}つ{当|あ}たりする (to take out one's anger on someone)

RELATED WORDS:
- {当|あ}たり{散|ち}らす (to lash out at everyone)
- {逆|さか}{恨|うら}み (misplaced resentment)

USAGE:
Often used with ～しないで or ～するな when telling someone not to take their frustration out on you. Common in contexts involving work stress, relationship problems, or general bad moods.
